newsitem.title: CANADA: Canfor to trim lumber output to meet quota.
newsitem.headline: Canfor to trim lumber output to meet quota.

text.p: Canfor Corp said Wednesday it tentatively planned to shut 10 of its sawmills for five days to stay within its lumber-export quota under a Canada-U.S. trade agreement.

A Canfor spokesman said nine of the mills would add five days of downtime to their normal three-day shutdown at Christmas. The 10th mill, at Grand Prarie, Alberta, is taking advantage of a current log shortage and shutting down for five days this week. It will close for three days at Christmas.
The spokesman said he did not know how much this would reduce the company's lumber output.

Canada and the United States reached a trade agreement last week that imposes a duty on Canadian softwood lumber exports once they exceed a certain threshold. This month Ottawa allocated the duty-free quota among Canadian producers.
Industry analysts have said that many producers received quotas that were 15 to 20 percent less than they had expected, which could reduce production around the end of the year.
